Welcome!
The Department of Astronomy at the University of Florida is home to a vibrant community actively engaged in research, education, and outreach. Our faculty lead a wide range of research programs using world-class resources including an in-house design-through-fabrication instrumentation program, partner level access to the Gran Telescope Canarias, the HiPerGator-3 supercomputer, and more. Our undergraduate and graduate programs host around 100 students who are split between our Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Arts, and Graduate Program. Our outreach program includes highly popular weekly public observing nights and annual Starry Night events which allow us to reach tens of thousands of community members.

A Trillion Mile Cosmic Stream of Gas Feeds GW Orionis
Friday August 7, 2026
A team of astronomers using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), of which the U.S. National Science Foundation National Radio Astronomy Observatory is a partner, has captured a massive stream of gas—one trillion miles, or .2 light years long—feeding the young triple-star system GW Orionis.
New study reveals potential atmosphere on rocky planet of nearby star
Monday July 20, 2026
Nearly a decade after discovering LHS 1140b, a rocky exoplanet in the habitable zone of a nearby low-mass star, a new study reveals the object may have its own atmosphere. UF undergraduate David Fulcher received an Honorable Mention for Chambliss Astronomy Achievement Student award

Student researchers from across the astronomy community presented their work in the Chambliss Astronomy Achievement Student Award poster competition at AAS 248 in Pasadena, California, in June 2026.

Researchers use James Webb Telescope to reveal hidden details of W51 star formation
Monday March 30, 2026
A team of University of Florida researchers used the James Webb Space Telescope to capture photos of a star-forming region known as W51 with never-before-seen clarity and resolution. The long wavelengths of JWST’s infrared technology allowed astronomers to see the stars clearly and show what was previously hidden.
UF researchers help capture most detailed view yet of the Milky Way’s core
Wednesday February 25, 2026
University of Florida astronomers helped create the largest and most detailed image ever made of the center of the Milky Way, giving scientists an unprecedented look at the raw material that forms new stars.
